cells.tense: You are standing at the open door and the shape of what's coming is already legible to you.
cells.act: gather the feelings that might be felt and look at them
cells.ask: Before deciding anything about what's arriving, collect every feeling it could bring — likely and unlikely alike — and look at the whole collection without picking among them yet.
cells.core:
Something is coming toward you now, and you can already see its shape before it fully lands. That's how your mind works — the pattern shows itself early and you read it true. On a good day this doesn't hurry to name what's arriving or what it means; it lets the pieces come in, and the reading holds. The door is open and you're standing in it well, letting what shows up be what it is.

What this balance can feed next is the pull of what might be felt, not the decision and not the plan. Before you sort what's arriving into what you'll do about it, let the possible feelings about it gather and just look at them — the ones you'd rather not have included too. Stay a minute longer than is comfortable. You don't have to choose among them. What you let gather will tell you what the reading is for.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the shape before the pieces finish arriving.
cells.verb: reading the pattern before the pieces have finished arriving
cells.place: the threshold where what was outside is entering now

cells.tense: What is arriving is being met with a verdict already drawn up before it has shown itself.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Take something that's arriving and settle what you'll do about it within the day — no reasons offered to anybody, no waiting for extra detail to come in and confirm the read.
cells.core:
Where you read what's coming, the reading has raced past the arrival. You see the pattern so early that you're already answering to next week's version of it, and the thing itself doesn't get to walk through the door before you've filed it. The clarity is real, but it's standing where patience used to be. What's entering now is being organized before it's been met.

There's another half to this, and it's this: make the call, then let the call carry itself. Not a new decision — one you're already sitting on. Settle it and move within the day, without laying out your reasons to anyone. A thing done well doesn't need announcing. What you're braced against will turn out to be smaller once you've moved through it than the bracing made it.

cells.tense: What is arriving has been standing at the threshold, and the door has stayed shut for some time.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Think of someone you've kept at a distance about something arriving, and walk one step toward them — say the one true thing, and leave out whatever doesn't carry it.
cells.core:
Where you read what's coming, the reading has gone quiet. Things arrive and you don't pick them up the way you used to; the pattern is there and you don't turn toward it. It isn't that something is missing in you. It's that you're standing a room away from the door, and the room has gotten comfortable. What's entering now is coming in without you meeting it, and somewhere you know that.

Meaning gets carried by people, by the ones who walk toward it and leave what no longer holds. So find someone who knows you and cross toward them with one true thing — something you've been keeping to yourself about what's arriving. Not everything. One thing, said plain. The walk is the work. You don't have to feel ready first.

cells.tense: The reading is happening, and you have been saying it belongs to anyone but you.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Notice something arriving that pulls at you, and follow the pull a little way this week — a small step toward it, no decision yet about whether it's yours to keep.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you're seeing its shape, and you keep filing it under circumstance — good timing, someone else's suggestion, just how things went. Nothing in that account carries your name. You gathered the pieces and saw how they fit before anyone else did, and the credit goes to luck or to the room. It reads as yours the moment you say so, and the ones near you already lean on how you take things in.

Before you decide anything about what's arriving, let the pull be the first thing you claim. Something draws you — follow it a little way this week. A small step, nothing after it. Not a plan; just going toward the pull and seeing what it looks like up close. That'll show you your hand in this faster than reasoning about it will.

attempts.check: The draft risks claiming the person has already seen a specific pattern that changed their understanding when the record only says pattern recognition is the capacity, not that a particular recognition has occurred, and it risks putting 'you're keeping everything possible' in their mouth — the reader could reasonably say I have no idea what's actually arriving or whether they feel anything about it. The asks survive being wrong: each is one small act that teaches something about the card's own capacity regardless of whether the read is right. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line that implies I know what's entering their life — I don't, and the cells should stay with the capacity, not with the content.
